newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close lower on flowback funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close lower on flowback funds.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed lower on Tuesday, reflecting the peak monthly period for money returning to the banking system following early-month outflows, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate closed below 6.0 percent at 5.968 against Monday's 6.081 finish, still outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.90-6.00 percent against 6.00.
Dealers said they expected the rates to remain stable in the near term on the central bank's recent issues of negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up excess liquidity.

In an apparent strategy to stave off overheating in the red-hot stock market, central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung said on Monday the bank would continue to issue NCDs to mop up banking system liquidity.
The central bank issued T$8 billion in NCDs on Tuesday afternoon.
The bond market remained in a consolidation, with the 10-year 86/4 bond yield at 6.1450 percent against 6.1425 and the seven-year 85/3 bond yield at 5.8700 against 5.8500.
